# Style transfer with FLUX.2

**Workflow:** [`flux2/flux2-style-transfer.json`](../flux2/flux2-style-transfer.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `flux2` |
| Nodes | 6 |
| Links | 4 |
| Paid API calls per run | **1** |

---

Two images into one FLUX.2 call: the first keeps its composition, the second lends its look, and the prompt says which is which.

**input_image** — the picture whose composition you keep.
**input_image_2** — the picture you take the look from.

Socket order matters. The prompt says "the first image" and "the second image", so swapping the two Load Image nodes reverses the effect.

`disable_pup` is **on**. FLUX.2 [pro] rewrites prompts by default and that rewrite tends to soften a precise instruction like this one. Turn it off if you would rather it embellish.

`width` / `height` are **0** — match the input image. Any other value must be at least 64.

Connect a third reference and a fourth socket appears, up to 8.

### Prompt shape that works
> Redraw the first image in the style of the second. Keep *(what stays)*. Take only *(what transfers)*.

Naming what must **not** change is what keeps the subject intact.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds every `prompt` field in this graph, so there is one
place to edit and the copies cannot drift apart, which matters here because the prompt is what tells the model which socket is which.

It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
